To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the afferent autoregulatory mechanism in the galactose fed rat is impaired.

1) the galactose diet, in addition to inducing polyol pathway activity, also produces renal autoregularory impairment; 2) the galactos-fed rat is a useful model to study the effects of increased polyol pathway metabolism independent of hyperglycaemia or insulin deficiency; and 3) increased polyol pathway metabolite accumulation may contribute to renal autoregulatroy impairment in diabetes mellitus.
afferent arteriolae in the galactose fed rats do not respond with constriction to increased pressure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the pathogenesis of renal autoregularory failure in diabetes mellitus.
the mechanisms responsible for impaired renal autoreguation in the diabetic rat, a condition that may contribute to diabetic nephropathy.
the role of the polyol pathway in diabetic nephropathy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
galactose feeding is associated with an impaired myogenic response of afferent glomerular arterioles, and this is associated with increased polyol pathway activation.
increased polyol metabolism is involved in the pathogenic process leading to the renal autoregulatoty defect observed in diabetes mellitus.
increased polyol metabolism may contribute to the renal autoregulative defect in diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the galactose model of diabetic renal injury is a good model for the study of diabetic renal disease.
polyol accumulation in renal afferent arteriolae contributes to the development of renal microvascular disease and renal failure in diabetes.
increased polyol metabolism is involved in the pathophysiological mechanisms of diabetic complications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

galactose-fed rats have a similar impairment of renal myogenic autoregulation as diabetic rats and that the galactose model of diabetes may provide an opportunity to explore the role of the polyol pathway on renal autoregula- tion.
the galactose model is a good model to study diabetic nephropathy.
galactose feeding can be used as a tool to study the role of polyol pathway activity in the pathophysiology of diabetic complications.
